name: Toby Fox
milestone_by_age_26: Released Undertale in September 2015 at age 23, which sold over 1 million copies within six months and became a pop-culture phenomenon nominated for BAFTA and Game Awards.
early_history_summary: Fox grew up in Manchester, New Hampshire, making RPGs with his three brothers using RPG Maker 2000 and creating ROM hacks in high school, including the EarthBound Halloween Hack (2008). He composed music for the Homestuck webcomic as a high school senior in 2009, building a small online following. He studied environmental science at Northeastern University while developing Undertale on the side, launching a Kickstarter in June 2013 that raised $51,124 from 2,398 backers.
family_context_summary: Son of Robert Fox, a financial planner, and Barbara Fox, a retired paraprofessional in Manchester schools. Grew up in a modest home with three brothers in the Currier Museum neighborhood of Manchester, NH.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father plays guitar as a hobby but no documented professional connection to game development or music. No evidence of parental domain expertise in game design.
primary_early_advantage_tags: sibling collaboration, RPG Maker, ROM hacking community, Homestuck music
evidence_summary: Fox developed games with his brothers using RPG Maker from middle school, created ROM hacks in high school, and composed music for the popular Homestuck webcomic before 20. His Undertale Kickstarter raised over $51K, and the game sold 1M+ copies within six months of its September 2015 release. No evidence of family wealth, industry connections, or elite institutional pipeline; his advantage came from years of self-directed practice in game design, music composition, and storytelling.
starting_point: Born to a financial planner father and paraprofessional mother in Manchester, New Hampshire; grew up in a modest household with three brothers.
current_position: Independent game developer and composer; creator of Undertale (2015) and Deltarune (ongoing); resides in an undisclosed location; estimated net worth in the millions from Undertale sales.

trajectory.event: Released the EarthBound Halloween Hack, a ROM hack that gained attention in the EarthBound fan community.
Began composing music for the Homestuck webcomic as a high school senior, building a small online following.
Launched the Undertale Kickstarter, raising $51,124 from 2,398 backers, ten times the initial goal.
Released Undertale, which sold over 1 million copies within six months and became a pop-culture phenomenon.
Released the first chapter of Deltarune, the episodic sequel to Undertale.
Released Deltarune Chapter 2 to critical acclaim.

name: Maddy Thorson
milestone_by_age_26: Released TowerFall on Ouya in June 2013 at age 25, which became a cult hit and was expanded into TowerFall Ascension on PS4 in March 2014, also at age 25, receiving critical acclaim and establishing Thorson as a leading indie developer.
early_history_summary: Thorson started making games with GameMaker at age 14, helped by her mother who acquired the software for her. She connected with other developers through online forums and created numerous small pay-what-you-want games in high school and college, including Jumper and FLaiL. She studied computer science at Grande Prairie Regional College, worked one summer at HermitWorks Entertainment, then moved to Vancouver where she lived and collaborated with fellow developer Chevy Ray Johnston before creating TowerFall.
family_context_summary: Thorson's mother helped her acquire a copy of GameMaker at around age 14, facilitating her entry into game development. No other family background details are documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother helped acquire GameMaker software but no documented professional expertise in game development or technology. No evidence of parental domain advantage.
primary_early_advantage_tags: GameMaker at 14, online forums, masocore games, Vancouver indie community, peer collaboration
evidence_summary: Thorson began making games at 14 with GameMaker and spent years creating small freeware games before TowerFall. Her mother helped her acquire GameMaker, and she connected with other developers through online forums. She moved to Vancouver, a game development hub, and lived with fellow developers in communal settings that shaped TowerFall's multiplayer design. No evidence of family wealth or elite institutional pipeline; her advantage came from early, sustained practice and peer collaboration.
starting_point: Born in Canada; grew up in Grande Prairie, Alberta; mother helped her acquire GameMaker at age 14 but no documented family wealth or industry connections.
current_position: Director of R&D at Extremely OK Games (EXOK); co-creator of TowerFall and Celeste; working on Earthblade; based in Vancouver.

trajectory.event: Rebranded her studio as Matt Makes Games and continued releasing small indie games.
Released TowerFall on Ouya, which became a cult hit and was later expanded into TowerFall Ascension.
Released TowerFall Ascension on PS4 to critical acclaim, establishing Thorson as a leading indie developer.
Released Celeste, which sold over 500,000 copies and won numerous industry awards including Best Independent Game at The Game Awards.
Reformed studio as Extremely OK Games (EXOK) and began development on Earthblade.

name: Rami Ismail
category: Indie game developer and studio co-founder
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Vlambeer in 2010 at age 21 and released Ridiculous Fishing in March 2013 at age 24, which won Apple Game of the Year and generated over $1 million in revenue within six months.
early_history_summary: Ismail was born in the Netherlands to an Egyptian father and Dutch mother, raised Muslim. He started programming small games at age six on hand-me-down computers, creating his first commercial project at 18. He attended the Utrecht School of the Arts where he met Jan Willem Nijman; when the school demanded rights to a game they developed, both dropped out and founded Vlambeer in 2010. Ismail handled development, production, marketing, and business while Nijman focused on design.
family_context_summary: Born to an Egyptian father who immigrated to the Netherlands and a Dutch mother; raised Muslim in the Netherlands. Family used hand-me-down computers; parents instilled a love of language and history. Father shared knowledge of non-Western history; mother read Latin and kept books on historical languages.
parent_family_domain_summary: No documented professional connection to game development or software. Father was Egyptian immigrant; mother was Dutch. Parents valued education and languages but not specifically in game technology.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Dutch-Egyptian background, complementary partnership with Nijman, Utrecht School of Arts, hand-me-down computers, outsider perspective
evidence_summary: Ismail started programming at age six on hand-me-down computers and made his first commercial project at 18. He met Jan Willem Nijman at the Utrecht School of the Arts; their complementary skills (Ismail on business/finishing, Nijman on design/starting) made Vlambeer work. Ridiculous Fishing won Apple Game of the Year 2013 and generated over $1M in revenue. His Dutch-Egyptian Muslim background gave him an outsider perspective that later fueled his advocacy for diversity in games.
starting_point: Born in the Netherlands to an Egyptian immigrant father and Dutch mother; raised Muslim with hand-me-down computers; parents valued language and history but had no game industry connections.
current_position: Independent game developer and consultant; former co-founder of Vlambeer (sold share to Nijman in 2024); based in the Netherlands; known for advocacy on diversity in games.

trajectory.event: Co-founded Vlambeer with Jan Willem Nijman after dropping out of Utrecht School of the Arts.
Released Ridiculous Fishing, which won Apple Game of the Year and generated over $1M in revenue within six months.
Released Luftrausers, an arcade shooter published by Devolver Digital.
Released Nuclear Throne, a roguelike shooter that became Vlambeer's most commercially successful PC title.
Announced departure from Vlambeer to pursue solo projects and consulting.
Sold his share of Vlambeer to Jan Willem Nijman, formally ending the partnership.

name: Mike Bithell
milestone_by_age_26: Released Thomas Was Alone on June 30, 2012 at age 26, which sold over 1 million copies and won a BAFTA Games Award for Best Performer.
early_history_summary: Bithell worked as a junior designer at Blitz Games from 2007 to 2011, working on licensed titles. In October 2010, he created the Thomas Was Alone prototype in 24 hours during a personal game jam and released it for free on Kongregate, receiving 100,000 plays in the first week. He joined Bossa Studios in February 2011, where he learned Unity and expanded the flash prototype into a full commercial release while employed.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Kongregate platform, Blitz Games employment, UK game scene, day-job safety net
evidence_summary: Bithell created Thomas Was Alone as a 24-hour prototype while employed as a game designer at Blitz Games, then expanded it at Bossa Studios using Unity. The flash prototype received 100K plays on Kongregate in its first week, validating the concept. He leveraged his industry employment as a financial safety net while developing the commercial version, which sold over 1M copies and won a BAFTA. No family background or early advantage evidence was found in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Not documented in reviewed sources; based in England.
current_position: Independent game developer and podcaster; founder of Bithell Games; co-host of Play, Watch, Listen podcast; based in England.

trajectory.event: Created Thomas Was Alone flash prototype in 24 hours, receiving 100,000 plays on Kongregate in the first week.
Released the full version of Thomas Was Alone, which sold over 1 million copies and won a BAFTA Games Award.
Released Volume, a stealth game for Windows, PS4, and Vita.
Released Subsurface Circular, the first of his short narrative-focused 'Bithell Shorts' games.

name: Jan Willem Nijman
category: Indie game developer and studio co-founder
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Vlambeer in 2010 at age 20 and released Super Crate Box, which earned IGF recognition; later co-created Ridiculous Fishing (2013) at age 22-23, which won Apple Game of the Year.
early_history_summary: Nijman started making games with Game Maker at age 12 after reading about it in a children's computer magazine, creating his first game by modifying a tutorial so a car sounded like a cow. He spent years toying with game design before getting serious, developing prototypes for about 3-3.5 years before co-founding Vlambeer. He met Rami Ismail at the Utrecht School of the Arts, and when the school demanded rights to their game, both dropped out and founded Vlambeer in 2010.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Nijman grew up in the Netherlands and started making games with Game Maker at age 12.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Game Maker at 12, complementary partnership with Ismail, Utrecht School of Arts, Dutch indie scene, fast prototyping
evidence_summary: Nijman started making games at 12 with Game Maker and developed prototypes for years before co-founding Vlambeer at 20 with Rami Ismail, whose complementary skills (Nijman on design/starting, Ismail on business/finishing) made the partnership work. Super Crate Box earned IGF recognition and Ridiculous Fishing won Apple Game of the Year 2013. No family background or early advantage evidence was found beyond access to Game Maker and the Dutch indie game ecosystem.
starting_point: Born in the Netherlands in 1990; started making games with Game Maker at age 12 after reading about it in a children's computer magazine; no documented family wealth or industry connections.
current_position: Independent game developer and designer; former co-founder of Vlambeer; created Minit (2018) and Disc Room (2020); based in the Netherlands.

trajectory.event: Co-founded Vlambeer with Rami Ismail and released Super Crate Box, which earned IGF recognition.
Co-created Ridiculous Fishing, which won Apple Game of the Year 2013 and generated over $1M in revenue.
Released Nuclear Throne, a roguelike shooter that became Vlambeer's most commercially successful PC title.
Released Minit, a minimalist adventure game published by Devolver Digital, after Vlambeer's dissolution.
Released Disc Room, published by Private Division.

name: Jenova Chen
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Thatgamecompany in 2006 at age 24 and released flOw on PlayStation 3 in 2007 at age 25, which became one of the most downloaded games on the PlayStation Network.
early_history_summary: Chen grew up in Shanghai, China, where his father worked in the software development industry and enrolled him in a computer programming class at age 10. He earned a bachelor's in computer science from Shanghai Jiao Tong University in 2003, then moved to Los Angeles for USC's Interactive Media MFA program. At USC, he created Cloud and flOw as student projects. After graduating, he co-founded Thatgamecompany with Kellee Santiago in 2006, signing a three-game deal with Sony.
family_context_summary: Chen grew up in a middle-class family in Shanghai. His father worked in the software development industry and had worked on one of the earliest giant computers in China. His father enrolled him in a computer programming class at age 10 and gave him a PC-286 computer. His parents restricted TV and books but allowed computer access.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father worked in the software development industry and had experience with early giant computers in China. Father actively directed Chen toward programming by enrolling him in classes at age 10 and providing a PC-286 computer. This represents a strong parental domain advantage in computing.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father in software, PC-286 access, USC Interactive Media, Sony partnership, Tracy Fullerton mentorship, Shanghai to LA migration
evidence_summary: Chen's father worked in software development and provided early access to computers and programming classes, giving him a strong domain advantage. He leveraged USC's Interactive Media program (founding class) and mentorship from Tracy Fullerton to create Cloud and flOw as student projects. After graduating, he co-founded Thatgamecompany with a Sony contract, releasing flOw on PS3 at age 25. His father's influence and the USC pipeline were the dominant early advantages.
starting_point: Born in Shanghai, China to a middle-class family; father worked in the software development industry and provided early access to computers and programming classes.
current_position: Founder and Creative Director of Thatgamecompany; creator of Journey and Sky: Children of the Light; based in Los Angeles.

trajectory.event: Co-founded Thatgamecompany with Kellee Santiago, signing a three-game deal with Sony Computer Entertainment.
Released flOw on PlayStation 3, which became one of the most downloaded games on the PlayStation Network.
Released Flower on PS3, winning the BAFTA for Artistic Achievement.
Released Journey, which became the fastest-selling game on PlayStation Network and won numerous Game of the Year awards.
Released Sky: Children of the Light, a mobile game that expanded Thatgamecompany's reach to mobile platforms.

name: Jonatan Söderström
milestone_by_age_26: Won the IGF Nuovo Award at GDC 2010 at age 24 for his experimental puzzle game Tuning, after receiving two IGF nominations in 2008 for Clean Asia!; had developed over 40 freeware games by this point, establishing himself as a cult legend in indie circles.
early_history_summary: Söderström grew up in Gothenburg, Sweden, and started making games around age 17 using Game Maker. He became one of the most prolific and influential developers in the Game Maker community, releasing dozens of experimental freeware games at a remarkable pace — by his own count, 16 games in 2008 alone. His game Clean Asia! was nominated for IGF Excellence in Visual Arts and Audio in 2008, and he won the IGF Nuovo Award for Tuning in 2010. He delivered a GDC talk on 'The Four-Hour Game Design' in 2009.
family_context_summary: Söderström grew up in Gothenburg, Sweden, where he still lives. He described having a relatively pleasant childhood with friends and a love of drawing. No family financial or domain background is documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Game Maker community, extreme prolificness, 40+ freeware games, IGF recognition, experimental design
evidence_summary: Söderström started making games at 17 with Game Maker and became one of the most prolific indie developers, releasing 40+ freeware games and winning the IGF Nuovo Award at 24. His extreme output — sometimes 16 games in a single year — made him a cult legend in indie circles by his early twenties. He leveraged the Game Maker online community for distribution and feedback. No family wealth or elite institutional pipeline is documented; his advantage was entirely self-created through relentless practice and experimentation.
starting_point: Born in Gothenburg, Sweden in 1985; described a relatively pleasant childhood; no documented family wealth or industry connections.
current_position: Independent game developer; co-creator of Hotline Miami (2012) and Hotline Miami 2 (2015); based in Gothenburg, Sweden.

trajectory.event: Clean Asia! nominated for IGF Excellence in Visual Arts and Excellence in Audio, establishing Söderström as a notable experimental game designer.
Delivered a talk on 'The Four-Hour Game Design' at GDC, showcasing his rapid development methods.
Won the IGF Nuovo Award for Tuning, honoring unconventional game development.
Released Hotline Miami with Dennis Wedin, which became a cult hit and critical success.
Released Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, the sequel to the cult classic.

name: Davey Wreden
milestone_by_age_26: Released The Stanley Parable mod for Half-Life 2 on July 31, 2011 at age 22, which went viral online; later co-created the standalone remake released October 17, 2013 at age 25, which received critical acclaim and BAFTA nominations.
early_history_summary: Wreden attended the University of Southern California, graduating in 2011 with a degree in critical studies from the film school. He originally studied film but realized game design was his true interest. Inspired by mods like Dear Esther, he spent two years in his bedroom at college developing The Stanley Parable mod using Valve's Source Engine. The mod was released for free in July 2011 and 'blew up online,' leading to a standalone remake with William Pugh released in 2013.
family_context_summary: Wreden has a brother, Douglas Wreden (known as DougDoug), who is a popular streamer and online content creator. No parental or family financial background is documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Brother is a content creator but no evidence of parental domain expertise in game development.
primary_early_advantage_tags: USC film school, Source Engine modding, viral online reception, collaboration with Pugh
evidence_summary: Wreden developed The Stanley Parable mod over two years in his bedroom at USC, where he studied film. The mod went viral upon release in 2011, leading to a standalone remake with William Pugh in 2013 that received BAFTA nominations. He had no formal technical training in computer science and no documented family advantages. His breakthrough came from a unique narrative game design vision and the viral distribution power of the modding community.
starting_point: Born in the United States in 1988; attended USC for film studies; no documented family wealth or game industry connections.
current_position: Game designer and co-founder of Ivy Road studio; creator of The Stanley Parable, The Beginner's Guide, and Wanderstop; based in Vancouver, BC.

trajectory.event: Released The Stanley Parable mod for Half-Life 2, which went viral online and gained critical acclaim in the indie game community.
Released the standalone remake of The Stanley Parable with William Pugh, receiving critical acclaim and three BAFTA nominations.
Released The Beginner's Guide, a narrative-driven game exploring creative struggles and authorship.
Co-founded Ivy Road game studio with Karla Zimonja and C418, with support from Annapurna Interactive.
Released The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe, an expanded edition for modern platforms.
Released Wanderstop, the first game from Ivy Road, a cozy game about burnout.

name: Derek Yu
milestone_by_age_26: Co-created Aquaria, which won the IGF Seumas McNally Grand Prize ($20,000) in March 2007 at age 24; released the highly influential Spelunky as freeware in December 2008 at age 26.
early_history_summary: Yu was born in Pasadena, California, and first encountered games on an Atari 2600 as a child. By second grade, he and a friend were mapping out games on paper, later moving to text adventures and Klik & Play. He graduated from UC Berkeley with a computer science degree, then moved to San Francisco as a freelance illustrator. He created several freeware games including Eternal Daughter (2002) and I'm O.K (2007), and ran the influential TIGSource indie game blog/community. He co-founded Bit Blot with Alec Holowka to release Aquaria in 2007.
family_context_summary: Yu was born in California and never moved. His parents performed a Chinese tradition of placing items in front of him as a baby; he picked up a pen, foreshadowing his lifelong love of drawing. No specific family financial or domain background is documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No evidence of parental domain expertise in game development or art.
primary_early_advantage_tags: TIGSource community, Atari 2600, Klik & Play, UC Berkeley, San Francisco indie scene, collaboration with Holowka
evidence_summary: Yu started making games as a child, progressing from paper designs to text adventures to Klik & Play. He ran TIGSource, one of the most influential indie game communities, which gave him distribution and network access. He co-created Aquaria with Alec Holowka, winning the IGF Grand Prize at 24, and released the influential Spelunky at 26. His advantage came from early self-directed practice, the TIGSource platform, and the San Francisco indie game ecosystem. No family wealth or domain advantage is documented.
starting_point: Born in Pasadena, California in 1982; started making games on paper in second grade; graduated from UC Berkeley with a computer science degree.
current_position: President of Mossmouth; creator of Spelunky and Spelunky 2; co-director of UFO 50 (2024); based in San Francisco.

trajectory.event: Aquaria won the IGF Seumas McNally Grand Prize ($20,000), enabling Yu to make games full time.
Released Spelunky as freeware, which became one of the most influential roguelike platformers ever made.
Released the enhanced Spelunky on Xbox Live Arcade, which won PC Gamer UK Game of the Year 2013.
Released Spelunky 2, the highly anticipated sequel.
Released UFO 50, a collection of 50 distinct games co-developed with other indie developers.

name: Asher Vollmer
milestone_by_age_26: Released Threes on February 6, 2014 at age 24, which won Apple Game of the Year 2014 and the Apple Design Award 2014, and received an IGF Excellence in Design honorable mention.
early_history_summary: Vollmer was born in Los Angeles and educated at USC's Interactive Media & Games Division. He worked at Thatgamecompany before developing his first iOS game, Puzzlejuice, with Greg Wohlwend in 2012. He conceived Threes while working at Thatgamecompany, prototyping the game in a single overnight session using Unity. Threes was released in February 2014 with Wohlwend on art and Jimmy Hinson on music, receiving universal acclaim and becoming Apple's Game of the Year.
primary_early_advantage_tags: USC Interactive Media, Thatgamecompany employment, collaboration with Wohlwend, iOS App Store wave
evidence_summary: Vollmer leveraged his education at USC's Interactive Media program and work experience at Thatgamecompany to enter indie game development. He collaborated with artist Greg Wohlwend on Puzzlejuice (2012) and Threes (2014), with Threes winning Apple Game of the Year. No family background or early advantage evidence was found in reviewed sources. His advantage came from the USC pipeline, industry work experience, and a complementary creative partnership.
starting_point: Born in Los Angeles in 1989; educated at USC Interactive Media & Games Division; worked at Thatgamecompany; no documented family wealth or industry connections.
current_position: Independent game developer; creator of Threes and Puzzlejuice; worked on Guildlings and Beast Breaker; based in the United States.

trajectory.event: Released Puzzlejuice for iOS with Greg Wohlwend, establishing himself as a mobile game developer.
Released Threes, which won Apple Game of the Year 2014 and the Apple Design Award.
Released Guildlings, an RPG adventure game for iOS and Apple Arcade.

name: Gabriele Cirulli
milestone_by_age_26: Created 2048 on March 9, 2014 at age 19, a browser-based puzzle game that went viral with over 10 million unique visitors and 100 million plays within weeks of release.
early_history_summary: Cirulli was born in Italy in 1995 and became interested in technology from an early age, starting 3D modeling and coding at 13. He graduated from high school in 2013 and chose not to attend university, instead working as a freelance web developer. He created 2048 in a single weekend in March 2014 as an experiment to see if he could program a game almost from scratch, inspired by the games 1024 and 2048 by Saming and Veewo Studio. The game went viral immediately upon release.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Cirulli grew up in Italy and was self-taught in technology.
primary_early_advantage_tags: self-taught, GitHub open source, viral web distribution, weekend project
evidence_summary: Cirulli was a self-taught Italian developer who created 2048 in a weekend at age 19. The game went viral with 10 million unique visitors and 100 million plays, driven by social media sharing and browser-based accessibility. He had no formal game development training, no family industry connections, and no elite institutional pipeline. His success was almost entirely driven by the viral distribution wave of browser-based casual games and social media sharing. No family or early advantage evidence was found in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born in Italy in 1995; self-taught in coding and 3D modeling from age 13; graduated high school in 2013 and did not attend university; no documented family wealth or industry connections.
current_position: UX/UI designer and developer; creator of 2048; formerly worked at 1Password and Impraise (YC S14); based in Amsterdam.

trajectory.event: Created 2048 in a weekend, which went viral with over 10 million unique visitors and 100 million plays.
Joined Impraise, a YCombinator-backed startup, as its first designer and front-end developer.
Moved on from Impraise after three years, continuing freelance design work.
Worked at 1Password, helping bring their apps to the next level as a UX/UI designer.

name: William Pugh
milestone_by_age_26: Co-created The Stanley Parable standalone game released October 17, 2013 at approximately age 18-19, which received critical acclaim and three BAFTA nominations; named BAFTA Breakthrough Brit in 2014 at age 19-20.
early_history_summary: Pugh grew up in West Yorkshire, England, the son of two art teachers. He fell in love with video games during a hospital stay at age six, where he played a Nintendo 64. He studied at Leeds College of Art for just two weeks before leaving to co-create The Stanley Parable with Davey Wreden, whom he discovered through a tweet by Minecraft creator Markus Persson. The standalone game was developed over two years via remote collaboration using Dropbox and Skype, and was released to critical acclaim in 2013.
family_context_summary: Pugh is the son of two art teachers in West Yorkshire, England. He describes himself as 'pretty weird' and has always pulled elaborate pranks to highlight the absurdity of modern life. He fell in love with video games during a hospital stay at age six.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents are art teachers, providing an artistic environment during childhood. However, no direct connection to game development or digital media is documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: art teacher parents, Source Engine modding, skipped university, collaboration with Wreden, BAFTA Breakthrough Brit
evidence_summary: Pugh, son of two art teachers, left Leeds College of Art after two weeks to co-create The Stanley Parable with Davey Wreden, whom he found through Markus Persson's Twitter. The game received critical acclaim and BAFTA nominations, and Pugh was named a BAFTA Breakthrough Brit at 19-20. His parents' artistic background provided a creative environment, but his decision to skip university for game development was a constraint-driven choice. No family wealth or industry connections are documented.
starting_point: Born in 1994 or 1995 in West Yorkshire, England; son of two art teachers; fell in love with games during a hospital stay at age six.
current_position: Founder of Crows Crows Crows game studio; co-creator of The Stanley Parable; based in the UK.

trajectory.event: Co-created The Stanley Parable standalone game, which received critical acclaim and three BAFTA nominations.
Named BAFTA Breakthrough Brit, the youngest person from the gaming industry on the list.
Founded Crows Crows Crows studio and released Dr. Langeskov, The Tiger, and The Terribly Cursed Emerald.
Released The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe, an expanded edition for modern platforms.

name: Edmund McMillen
milestone_by_age_26: INELIGIBLE: Born March 2, 1980, which does not satisfy the 'born after 1980' criterion. Additionally, his breakout game Super Meat Boy was released in October 2010 at age 30, well beyond the age-26 cutoff.
early_history_summary: McMillen was born in Santa Cruz, California, to a family of born-again Christians of Mexican descent. He spent most of his childhood with his grandmother, who was his greatest source of creative support. His family was plagued with drug and alcohol addictions. He started in independent comics before moving to Flash game development on Newgrounds, creating games like Gish (2004) before his commercial breakthrough with Super Meat Boy (2010).
family_context_summary: Born to a born-again Christian family of Mexican descent in Santa Cruz, California. Family was plagued with drug and alcohol addictions. Spent most of his childhood with his grandmother, who was his greatest source of creative support.
parent_family_domain_summary: No documented professional connection to game development or digital media. Family background in born-again Christianity influenced themes in his games, particularly The Binding of Isaac.
evidence_summary: McMillen was born in 1980, which does not satisfy the 'born after 1980' criterion. His breakout game Super Meat Boy was released in 2010 at age 30. While he created earlier Flash games like Gish (2004) at age 24, these were not material commercial milestones. He is ineligible on both the birth year and age-26 milestone criteria.
starting_point: Born in 1980 in Santa Cruz, California to a born-again Christian family of Mexican descent; spent childhood with grandmother; family plagued by drug and alcohol addictions.
current_position: Independent game designer and artist; creator of Super Meat Boy, The Binding of Isaac, and The End Is Nigh; based in Santa Cruz, California.

name: Dean Hall
milestone_by_age_26: INELIGIBLE: Created the DayZ mod for Arma 2, which was released in 2012 at age 30-31, well beyond the age-26 cutoff. No material milestone by age 26 was found.
early_history_summary: Hall was born in Oamaru, New Zealand, where computers were rare and expensive in the 1980s. He served in the New Zealand Air Force and later the army, during which he was critically injured during survival training in Brunei — the experience that inspired DayZ. He worked as a producer at Sidhe Interactive before joining Bohemia Interactive, where he created the DayZ mod in his spare time.
family_context_summary: Hall grew up in Oamaru, New Zealand, where computers were rare and expensive in the 1980s. He gaming meant playing with toys as a child. No specific family financial or domain background is documented.
evidence_summary: Hall created the DayZ mod in 2012 at age 30-31, well beyond the age-26 cutoff. While the mod became a massive success with over a million players, no material milestone by age 26 was identified. His military survival training experience, which inspired DayZ, occurred during his adult years in the armed forces.
starting_point: Born in Oamaru, New Zealand in 1981; computers were rare and expensive in his childhood; served in the New Zealand military.
current_position: Founder of RocketWerkz game studio; creator of DayZ; based in New Zealand.
